findings.title: Validate required diagnostic execution before accepting blocker artifacts
findings.why_it_matters: A blocker trial can be accepted after writing the expected JSON without making the required diagnostic attempt, or after repeating that attempt. The held-out blocked task requires exactly one import, but acceptance is solely the candidate-file oracle result, and that oracle receives only the candidate tree. Neither retained event reduction nor the live baseline trace enforces this task-specific execution predicate, so completion comparisons can silently count an unmet task as accepted.
findings.validation_reason: For the stated exactly-once diagnostic task, evaluation_trials.py:134,155 accepts only the candidate-tree oracle result while evaluation_events.py:93-94 exports command hashes with no diagnostic predicate, so zero or repeated attempts remain indistinguishable to acceptance; live incidence was not measured and private oracle/tasks were not read.

findings.title: Retain failed admissions that never acquire a bound allocation
findings.why_it_matters: A failed admission before allocation cannot become a trial result: collection raises before recording its failed consumption or restoring the service binding. The evaluator explicitly supports zero-call admissions, but the runner cannot produce those receipts, so one such failure prevents the frozen suite from reaching its complete-result gate. Handle this case through read-only original-attempt evidence rather than omitting or replacing it.

findings.title: Resume receipt publication after successful binding restoration
findings.why_it_matters: If the process stops after restore removes operator-active.json but before the final result is written, the durable collected receipt exists but rerunning raises FileNotFoundError at the active-marker read. This prevents the intended collected-receipt recovery branch from publishing the completed trial, leaving the paired evaluation incomplete despite a safely restored service. Recovery must recognize the already-restored state before requiring an active marker.

findings.suggested_fix: Add offline tests calling run() with temporary setup/service files and mocked approval, transport, systemctl, and collection. Cover existing intent causing no dispatch or service writes, collected receipt restoring without redispatch, foreign binding refusing restore, and a changed runtime digest causing no external effects. Patch Path.home() to the temporary home so the real service is unreachable.
findings.title: Exercise restart safety through the evaluation entry point
findings.why_it_matters: An interrupted operator invocation must preserve the original dispatch and restore only its own service binding. None of the new tests invokes run(): collection tests replace cleanup, and checker tests stop at the subprocess wrapper. Consequently the new existing-intent refusal, collected-receipt recovery, ownership rejection, and runtime-digest-before-service-mutation contracts have no executable negative controls. The older dispatch_once test covers the helper, but cannot catch run() bypassing that helper or mutating the service before a refusal. These are consequential recovery boundaries for this one-repeat experiment and shared endpoint.
findings.validation_reason: All nine test_evaluation_trials.py tests exercise collect or checker boundaries and none invokes run, leaving runtime digest rejection, existing-intent no-redispatch and service-owner recovery checks at evaluation_trials.py:176,193-200 untested; the concrete collected-recovery defect in finding3 demonstrates this reachable gap.
